master_narrator.agency_handoff_prompt:
The table was silent. Not the good, tired silence of a job well done. The sharp, brittle silence of sixteen people who had been breathing the same recycled air for too long.

Elias sat at the end of the long timber board, his hands folded over a leather-bound notebook. His task was to archive the linguistic and epistemic memory of the sixteen so nothing true is lost, carefully tracking the fragile social ecosystem of their found-family fellowship. But tonight, the ecosystem was collapsing. The Third-Quarter isolation micro-stressors had accumulated past the breaking point, compounding into a near mutiny simply because Kaio filtered the dinner's soup stock through a sock.

Kaio defended his engineering marvel with wide-eyed sincerity, waving the offending garment like a banner. A vein pulsed visibly in Ryn's temple. Elias watched the micro-expressions ripple across the room—the clamped jaws, the rigid spines, the elevated heart rates. Mitigating Isolated-Confined-Extreme (ICE) Third-Quarter cortisol cascades and autonomic hypervigilance required structured communal roast rituals and oxytocin vagal buffering. Instead, they had a sock in the broth.

Ryn slammed a ladle against the cast-iron pot. The metallic ring severed the argument, bouncing off the brushed brass and ironwood bulkheads. Elias flinched, the sudden sharp noise jarring his spine. He leaned back, his shoulders squaring as his Taurus override engaged. The quiet observer dug his heels in with immovable, deadpan stubbornness. He pushed his chair back a single inch, scraping the floorboards to draw focus.

"If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong," Elias said, his voice flat, completely devoid of inflection.

Silence rushed back in. Sixteen pairs of eyes snapped toward him.

"It was a clean sock," Kaio offered weakly.

Elias stared straight ahead, his expression carved from stone. "A clean sock in a mycelial reduction broth implies a radical approach to textile-integrated gastronomy. It is a bold paradigm shift."

Vex choked on a mouthful of water. A small, involuntary snort escaped Zara. The brittle tension fractured. Elias held his ground, maintaining his stoic expression as the absurdity of the situation washed over the crew. The cortisol cascades halted, replaced by the vagal buffering of shared, reluctant amusement.

Sixteen mugs raised in the warm circle of firelight while the captured geode hums beneath the floorboards. The crisis had passed. Therefore, Elias turned his gaze toward the end of the table, offering a small, imperceptible nod.

Elara stood up, collecting the empty bowls. "Right," she announced, "next time, use a sieve. Who wants seconds?"
